issues.title: audit(phase): the CLASS behind #1134 -- 0 new reachable permalocks, 1 live silent-loss defect, and a guard proven red against the real thing
issues.body:
Answers Pip's 2026-08-06 question after the #1134 playtest:

> "removing the feature is correct but I think the phase guard thing is very good and we should think about if anything else in the game needs it?"

Not about #1134. **PR #1143's removal is the ruled fix for the instance** and nothing here duplicates or contradicts it. This is the audit of the CLASS.

## Headline counts, stated separately as asked

| | |
|---|---|
| Phase-critical state variables enumerated | **10** |
| Mutation sites classified | **34** |
| CONFIRMED reachable silent permalocks | **3** -- all already deleted by PR #1143 |
| CONFIRMED reachable permalocks OUTSIDE #1143's scope | **0** |
| CONFIRMED non-permalock defects (live, reported, not fixed) | **1** |
| THEORETICAL hazards with no production route | **3** |

I would rather hand back 0 new permalocks with the reachability arguments written out to be attacked than 40 theoretical ones. Every "cleared" writer in the doc carries the argument that cleared it.

## The mechanism is not where the brief said it was

The brief named `turn_manager.gd:895` (`can_select_actions = pending_events.size() == 0`). That line is real but **read by nothing shipped** -- it is a Dictionary field whose only consumers are two assertions in `test_turn_manager.gd`. The live lock is a three-part interlock:

1. `GameManager.select_action:185` hard-refuses while `pending_events` is non-empty.
2. `TurnManager.resolve_event:862` refuses unless `current_phase == TURN_START`; the month-loop's alternative drain only engages when `month_controller.is_paused()`.
3. The `event_triggered` modal is `PRIORITY_MUST_ANSWER`, ESC-proof (#452), and since the 2026-07-24 "direction-b" change closes **only on a successful resolve**.

So the sharper invariant, which generalises past `pending_events`:

> **INVARIANT E.** `event_triggered` may only be emitted when a resolution path can succeed -- `is_paused()`, or `current_phase == TURN_START`, or the synthetic month-review id.

Violate the queue invariant alone: a mute, often recoverable run. Violate E as well: **dead**. #1134 did both, which is why it read as a hard lock.

Non-obvious half, worth Pip's attention: **the escape hatch exists and is covered up.** `COMMIT PLAN` -> `end_month()` auto-appends `PASS_ACTION_ID` on an empty queue -> `advance_tick` -> `start_turn` -> `pending_events.clear()`. A player who could click that button would have unlocked their own run. The modal blocker is what makes the defect terminal.

## The one live defect I found and did NOT fix

**`TurnManager._step_check_events:541`** does `state.pending_events = triggered_events` -- a whole-array **replace**. `SeedSchedule.inject_event` (`seed_schedule.gd:56`) appends earlier in the same `start_turn`. So **a scenario-authored `inject_event` is silently destroyed whenever a random event fires the same turn.** Silent content loss, exactly the repo's documented failure mode.

Not fixed per the brief: it changes which events fire on a seed, which forks every recorded replay and moves league results. Pip's call.

## Recommended mechanism, and what it MISSES

Weighed four options (shared assertion helper / phase-aware private setter / test-time scanner / documented invariant). **Recommend the test-time scanner, installed here**, with phase-aware setters recorded as the real fix and deferred.

The argument against the assertion helper generalises past this repo: **an opt-in guard is guarded by the discipline it is meant to replace.** `debug_overlay.gd:435` *already had* a guard -- `if not gm or not gm.state: return`. The author was guarding. They guarded the wrong variable.

Against private setters: better on paper, but ~34 call sites, several in `turn_manager`/`replay_simulator` whose write ORDER *is* the deterministic RNG stream ("STEP ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING"), and GDScript has no `private` so enforcement collapses back to a scan anyway.

**Blind spots of what I installed, stated so they are not mistaken for coverage:**

- It cannot tell a safe write from an unsafe one **inside** an allowlisted file. `turn_manager.gd` is allowlisted and the defect above lives in it. **The scanner is green on a live bug.** That is the honest boundary.
- Static: aliases, `call()`, `set("pending_events", ...)` all pass through.
- The allowlist is a permissive superset, so it will not notice a #1143-style removal regressing (#1143 ships its own guard for that -- complementary, not redundant).

A **runtime** invariant check was prototyped and **rejected**: that state combination occurs legitimately inside `advance_tick`, between `start_turn` returning a `SeedSchedule` injection and `:100` clearing it. A guard that false-fires in normal play trains people to ignore it.

## Red/green proof, measured both ways

`godot/tests/unit/test_phase_critical_state_guard.gd` -- 7 tests, including three backstops (the #640 lesson) and two that fail if the drain-path refusals this whole audit rests on are ever relaxed.

All runs: `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300`.

**Baseline** (`origin/main` @ `78be0370`, before any change):
```
[PASS] 'quick': 1146 tests, 0 failures, 112/112 files collected.
```

**RED** -- tombstone allowlist entries temporarily removed, i.e. run against the live #1134 defect:
```
[FAIL] 'quick': 1153 tests, 2 failures, 113/113 files collected.

test_only_audited_files_mutate_phase_critical_state
  res://scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:445 mutates state.pending_events -- gm.state.pending_events.append(event)
  res://scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd:485 mutates state.pending_events -- gm.state.pending_events.append({"id": event_id, "scheduled": true})

test_event_triggered_is_emitted_only_from_audited_files
  res://scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:449 -- gm.emit_signal("event_triggered", event)
```
All three #1134 sites named unprompted, from an enumeration built before the offenders were looked at.

**GREEN** -- tombstone entries restored (legitimate on this base; the allowlist is permissive so **#1143 merges green**):
```
[PASS] 'quick': 1153 tests, 0 failures, 113/113 files collected.
```

1146 -> 1153 = +7, matching the 7 new tests. 112 -> 113 files = +1.

### The guard was hollow on its first run

Worth reading, because it nearly proved its own point against itself. The first draft compiled, ran, and reported 1 failure -- looking like a working guard. It was not: the receiver regex excluded a preceding `.`, so `gm.state.pending_events.append(event)` -- *the actual #1134 line* -- matched **nothing**, and the allowlist test passed green with the offenders removed from the allowlist. Only the separate `event_triggered` regex fired, which is what made the discrepancy visible. Fixed, and `test_scanner_finds_the_known_offender_shape` now pins the shape with literals so it cannot recur. Written up in the doc, not buried.

## Merge-order note

The two `PENDING_REMOVAL_1143` allowlist entries and the `debug_overlay` emitter entry exist only because #1143 had not merged when this branch was cut. The allowlist is permissive, so **merge order does not matter**. After #1143 lands, delete those three entries.

## Follow-ups deliberately left for Pip

| Item | Why not done |
|---|---|
| `_step_check_events` clobbering scheduled injections | forks replays, moves league results |
| Force `TURN_START` on load when pending events survive rehydrate | changes loaded-run behaviour; save-version policy |
| Delete `state.can_end_turn` (9 writers, **0 readers** -- a gate that gates nothing) | touches the save schema |
| Delete dead `GameManager.end_turn()` (unreferenced outside tests) | simulation-tier tests exercise it |
| Phase-aware setters | ~34 sites, load-bearing step order |

issues.body:
Answers Pip's 2026-08-06 question -- "200 issues open and none of them being worked on?" -- with a full triage of all 201 open issues, plus an eight-fix drive-by batch.

## Part 1 -- the triage (the deliverable)

`docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE_2026-08-06.md`. Headline counts:

| Bucket | Count |
|---|---|
| DONE ALREADY (verified against code) | 8 |
| DONE ALREADY (likely; one check each) | 15 |
| STALE / OVERTAKEN | 19 |
| DRIVE-BY fixed in THIS PR | 8 |
| DRIVE-BY still available | 8 |
| NEEDS PIP | 27 |
| REAL WORK | 116 |
| **Total** | **201** |

**The single biggest reason the pile is not moving:** squash-merge never fires closes-keywords here (CLAUDE.md documents it), so every landed fix leaves its issue open unless someone closes it by hand. 23+ of the 201 are closed-in-fact-but-open-on-GitHub. The counter only ever goes up, so the pile LOOKS static while 100+ commits landed since 07-26.

Also flagged: **#1061 (IP/trademark) was DUE 2026-08-03 and is still open.** Pip asked to be forced.

## Part 2 -- the eight fixes

1. **#1062** Leaderboard Duration column DELETED (header node + row label + dead `_format_duration`). Score is turns survived; wall-clock next to the ranking rewarded fast clickers. Display-only: `duration_seconds` still recorded/submitted (contract frozen per website #191).
2. **#1035** The last two authored non-ASCII strings in `.tscn` (real arrow glyphs in leaderboard pagination) replaced with ASCII, and `scripts/check_no_emoji.py` now enforces full ASCII on authored `.tscn` string properties (`text`/`tooltip_text`/`placeholder_text`, multiline included) so the gap cannot reopen. **Guard proven failing first:** run against the pre-fix tree it exited 1 with exactly `leaderboard_screen.tscn:189 U+2190` and `:199 U+2192`; green after the fix.
3. **#700** Local `Leaderboard.add_score` now dedupes by `entry_uuid` (mirrors the remote PHP `duplicate:true`). **Second guard proven:** the pre-existing characterization test asserting the no-dedup behaviour failed on all 6 seeds when the fix landed (`test_leaderboard_properties.gd:121`), then was flipped to assert full idempotency (size unchanged + `duplicate=true`).
4. **#1032** ENTER double-fire on the launch screen: `config_confirmation._input` now marks ENTER/KP_ENTER handled (press AND release -- BaseButton fires on release) so `increment_games_played()` runs once per keyboard launch instead of twice.
5. **#1029** Cold-open replay: `GameConfig.reset_intro_seen()` + a "Replay story intro" button on the settings operations board (Col2, under the intros toggle), with visible confirmation.
6. **#882** Bug-report auto-close now shows a visible "Closing in N..." countdown instead of a silent 6-second wait; bails cleanly if the panel is closed/reused mid-count.
7. **#1134** F3 event injection now has a phase guard: injection is refused outside ACTION_SELECTION (the only phase where `pending_events` still drains), with a legible refusal dialog + warning instead of a permalocked run. Guard is static/pure; new `test_debug_inject_phase_guard.gd` covers all four phases exhaustively (and trips if `TurnPhase` ever gains a member).
8. **#1064** The leaderboard's "Play Again" button -- which reads as a lie when no game was played ("there wasn't a game to play again from") -- is now "New Run" with a tooltip. It always went to pregame setup; now the label says so. (The residual ask -- auditing every post-run route -- is noted in the triage as real work.)

Dropped as instructed: **#1085** (minimise does not minimise). Investigated inside the timebox: `project.godot` launches `window/size/mode=2` (maximized) and the project has no specified minimise/restore behaviour at all; the #1079 badge-refit callback shows no mechanism that could block a minimise. Undiagnosable without a live repro; recommend folding into **#820** (window mode options) as the fix vehicle -- triage doc says the same.

Skipped on purpose: **#1086** (onboard-now tooltip) because the missing Attention cost may live in the costs dict itself, which grazes sim behaviour -- flagged in the triage instead.

## Issues that should CLOSE on merge (do not auto-close; evidence in the triage doc)

issues.title: fix(debug): retire the debug event-trigger -- delete the feature, not guard it (#1134)
issues.body:
Closes #1134 -- **by removing the feature, not by fixing it.**

## Pip's ruling (2026-08-06, after a release-build playtest)

> "the hard lock from popping an event in the wrong screen was repeatable so that might just be something we disable or put on the back burner for now, triggering random events doesn't seem so useful for debugging at this point, just creating bugs lol."

He reproduced the permalock repeatably and judged the feature's debugging value lower than its bug-creation cost. So this PR deletes the debug event-trigger rather than making it phase-safe. #1134 closes as "feature retired", not "bug fixed" -- there is nothing left to be phase-unsafe.

## The defect, verified against the code

`debug_overlay._trigger_specific_event()` appended a raw event dict onto `gm.state.pending_events` behind nothing but `if not gm or not gm.state: return`. **No phase guard.** `TurnManager` gates `can_select_actions` on `pending_events.size() == 0`, so an injection made in a phase that never drains the queue left the run permanently unplayable.

The overlay is instanced unconditionally in `main.tscn` (~line 415) and its keybind is bound in `_ready` with no build check, so this was reachable by any player in a shipped build, not only in dev.

## Sibling unguarded writer -- found and retired too

`dev_mode_overlay.gd` (ALPHA TOOLS, backslash) carried the identical shape: an event dropdown, "Queue selected event" and "Trigger random event", all routing through `_queue_event()` -> `gm.state.pending_events.append(...)` with no phase guard. That overlay is *also* reachable in release builds (gated on `BuildInfo.are_alpha_tools_available()` since PR #1079/#1104, deliberately). Same trivially-removable shape, and Pip's words name random event injection specifically, so it went with the F3 button.

No other dev/debug surface writes to `pending_events`. `SeedSchedule.inject_event` does, but that is core sim, not a dev surface -- left alone.

## Removed

- `debug_overlay.gd`: `_on_trigger_event_button_pressed`, `_show_event_selection_popup`, `_trigger_specific_event`, plus the already-dead `event_dropdown` / `event_trigger_container` fields
- `debug_overlay.tscn`: the `TriggerEventButton` node and its `pressed` connection
- `dev_mode_overlay.gd`: the dropdown / two buttons / note in the TRIGGERS section, `_populate_event_dropdown`, `_queue_event`, `_queue_selected_event`, `_trigger_random_event`, the `_event_dropdown` field
- Two stale doc lines in `godot/ERROR_HANDLING_QUICK_REFERENCE.md` and `godot/OPTION_E_ERROR_HANDLING_COMPLETE.md`

Left intact: the read-only inspection (the F3 readout still prints the pending-events queue -- looking is free, touching is not), the resource nudges, the day-step, the jumps. Tombstone comments at both sites say what was removed and why.

## Regression guard, proved red then green

New `godot/tests/unit/test_no_debug_event_injection.gd` (4 tests):

1. the scan actually finds files (backstop against a hollow guard -- the #640 lesson)
2. no `.gd` under `scripts/debug` **mutates** `pending_events` (comment-stripped source scan; reads such as `.size()` stay legal)
3. none of the retired symbol names reappears
4. `debug_overlay.tscn` carries no trigger-event control or connection

**Red run** (guard added, feature still present) -- 3 failures, naming both offenders unprompted:

```
res://scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:445: gm.state.pending_events.append(event)
res://scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd:485: gm.state.pending_events.append({"id": event_id, "scheduled": true})
...
debug_overlay.gd defines/calls retired symbol _on_trigger_event_button_pressed  (+6 more)
...
debug_overlay.tscn still carries the retired Trigger Event button (#1134)
```

```
[FAIL] 'quick': 1150 tests, 3 failures, 113/113 files collected.
```

**Green run** (after removal):

```
[PASS] 'quick': 1150 tests, 0 failures, 113/113 files collected.
[SUCCESS] All requested suites passed the gate!
```

Test count: 1146 before this PR, 1150 after (the new file adds 4). Measured both times with `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300`.

## Note for Pip (out of scope, not touched)

`docs/CONTROLS.md:53` documents the debug overlay on `~`; the actual keybind is **F3** (`keybind_manager.gd:22`). Stale, but unrelated to this change -- say the word and it gets its own one-liner.

issues.title: Playthrough of this afternoon's build: music works, save looks better -- but settings traps you into quitting, F3 will not close, and the cold open never fired
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memo `2026-08-06_140157__c11e34d1`, recorded 14:01 AEST playing **the fresh build made this afternoon** — *"was meant to be fixing a few things."* Live play, narrated as it happened. Transcribed locally; quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated.

## Core message

**The music system works and the save looks much better.** Two navigation defects made him quit the game entirely to get out of a menu, and **the cold open did not fire on any of three attempts**, so it remains unverified rather than working.

## Two navigation defects, one of which forced a quit

**1. Settings has no exit except "back to game" — so from the main menu it is a trap.**

> I can't go from settings to quit, I can only go back to game. So now if I go back to game, I have to quit. **I'm just going to quit out entirely, that sucked.**

Reached from the main menu, Settings offers a route that assumes a game is running. He had to close the application.

**2. `F3` does not toggle, and the overlay cannot be dismissed.**

> clicking F3 again doesn't work, clicking out of F3 using the X works, backslash doesn't bring anything up

So `F3` opens but does not close, and one documented dismissal path is dead while another works.

## The cold open did not fire — three attempts

He tried the sequence three times, twice deliberately re-entering via settings to enable story entries:

> Settings, all protocols, play story entries on, front card, back to game — that's not going to work. Main menu, launch lab, launch lab... **I did not get the intro, so I can't confirm whether the intro worked or not.**

**Treat the cold open as unverified, not as working.** Whatever the fresh build changed, he could not reach it. Worth checking whether the story-entries setting actually gates it, and whether it persists across the settings round-trip he was forced into by defect 1.

## Music — works, one refinement

Confirmed working after some confusion: *"Excellent, okay — no, the music works."* Selecting a track and pressing play works; selecting a second and playing switches correctly.

**The one fix:** *"we need to make it more clear that the track is fading over and that it takes a few seconds"* — the crossfade reads as unresponsiveness. He was otherwise enjoying it.

## Player guide — better, one structural note

*"How to play is good, the month is good, attention and resources"* — all fine, and he likes that money, compute, research papers and reputation are now **coloured**, with a caveat: *"I don't know if those colourings are consistent, but if they are then that's kind of cool."* **Worth confirming those four colours are used consistently everywhere**, because he is about to rely on them.

Structural note: *"these are all scrollable little mid-sections, as opposed to one long continuous scroll, which is weird."*

## Leaderboard — a concrete request

> it would be cool on the leaderboards to be able to **sort them — by date, or duration, or turns** — just have that dropdown filter once the information is loaded.

Sorting client-side after load, not a new query. This composes with the leaderboard work in the teardown response.

## Small observations

**Staff cards grow slightly on click** when planning to interview — *"a weird little on-click effect"*, noted as funny rather than wrong.

**The phase-one event error is now handled.** Previously this produced an unrecoverable state; now *"I get a nice little error message in the background."* Still cannot resolve, but it no longer traps him — the earlier report in `#1132` can be considered improved, though the underlying dev-tool boundary question stands.

## Not tested, deliberately

He intended to test offline behaviour and decided against it mid-session: *"I'm not going to turn off the network because I'm just doing too many other things, we'll deal with that other thing later."* **Network-loss behaviour remains untested.**

issues.title: Pip's full response to the Fresh Eyes Teardown (26 min, from memory) -- meta dev cycle, month review becomes an expandable action log, winning does not exist
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memo `2026-08-06_134936__401fbe0b` — **26 minutes**, recorded 13:23 AEST from memory, not at a screen: *"I'm just doing this sitting in my bedroom, I'm not looking at a screen but I'm visually recreating things."* Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated.

## Core message

**He rated the teardown itself as exceptional** — *"that is an exceptional document, I was very pleased with that"* — and responded to essentially all of it. Two things below are bigger than the items that produced them: a **meta dev cycle** for rotating his own attention across the game, and a redesign of the **month review into an expandable action log** that he worked out live in the recording.

He closed with: *"take all this half an hour of rambling and see what we can do with it."*

## The two structural ideas

### 1. A meta dev cycle, borrowing the coordination status vocabulary

> now that we've got the attention / drifting / lost mechanisms through the coordination repo, we should be able to think about **how I apply those to segments of the game**, so that I'm turning my attention to bits of it in waves... at the moment my attention goes away from something and **I don't have anything to specifically draw it back**.

His sketch: **music → UX → UI → customer experience → scoreboards**, rotating on roughly a **six-to-eight week** cycle, running alongside normal work.

> otherwise I'm going to be splitting my attention in so many different ways it's going to be wild.

This is `§5c` (`coordination#22`) applied to game areas rather than work items. **A game area can be `starved` exactly like a ticket can**, and the cycle is the mechanism that un-starves it on a schedule rather than on a crisis. Composes with the tech-debt cadence question already raised in `#1138`.

### 2. Month review becomes an expandable action log — worked out live

He starts sceptical of the month review — *"I'm not actually sure if the month review is actually relevant... right now all of it is low information value"* — and then arrives somewhere else mid-sentence (*"right, aha, there we go"*):

- **Not a popup.** Overlay it on screen regions that are no longer relevant.
- **Summary first, detail on demand.** Click any line to expand into the action log. *"which lets the player manage information density."*
- **Navigation is two-way and lossless.** Summary → ledger → back to summary. During planning you can still review last month. *"The flow of information should be pretty comfortably lossless"*, and you lose the previous turn only once you start a new one.
- **Never make the player click accept twenty times.** *"you just go boop, give me the summary."*
- **The summary's quality can itself be a game variable:** *"you only get the information that the game has given you, which means what the month summary is is basically possibly even reflected in the quality of the player's UI upgrades."*

His analogy for what good looks like: *"imagine a good operating system where you can click into — hey, there were these five crises that fired off — like an API dashboard."*

**Related, and part of the same loop:** a **persistent office simulator on both screens** that does not update during planning, then visibly plays out as the action queue drains — *"you're getting to see the reward of your decisions paying off, which closes a visual feedback loop."* He compares the queue to Magic's stack (not strictly FIFO) and suggests colour-coding cards, size differences, showing trade-offs.

Self-aware footnote, worth keeping: *"some people will be like, Pip, you're just recreating a fucking Kanban board from first principles, and I'll say no, it came from a game, I was inspired by a game not the other way round. Oh dear, it's entirely possible this is true."*

## Rulings

**Winning does not exist.** Settled. *"These things are old, they're bad, get rid of it — bad bad bad."* Remove the surfaces that imply otherwise.

**Bug-report friction is unacceptable.** *"Not being able to submit a bug report, or having the friction of a manual step, is so fucking stupid. I don't ever want to expose a player to it again."*

**The main-menu start verb is wrong.** Not "launch lab". Wants a **quick start** plus **prepare lab** (or configure lab), with prepare lab as the main path.

**Menu cleanup.** Key bindings → into settings, drop the button. AI safety info → under a **resources** section. Player guide is broken and known; fix later.

**Bottom buttons: remove them.** *"I think we should just get rid of all the buttons and shit down the bottom"* — they invite clicks that break things.

**The 10-pixel hint line** — *"fucking terrible, let's make that like a 50-pixel hint line and just make all the text much bigger. We've got a lot of useless space on the screen."*

**Tile titles shown by default** for new players, under the icons, hideable via UI options — ideally offered after a few turns (*"hey, you can hide this"*).

**Icons:** smaller up top, **chunkier action buttons** with more room and weight. Open question he flagged rather than resolved: Civ and AoE put resources top-static, but *"you're also moving a screen around"* and pdoom's screen is mostly static — unclear what that changes.

**Empty-queue commit needs a soft confirm**, not just auto-pass: *"you are committing an empty queue, you have no actions planned for this month and you're fully reserving your attention — is that what you wish to do?"* First couple of times only. His reference: it is Magic's *untap, upkeep, draw, go* — legal, but you would normally do something.

**The mode banner + phase label pair is good but ugly.** *"the thing at the top is good, so we just need to make it look more like a UI and less like a couple of bits of text that we jammed in."*

**Approved as good:** cold open structure, commit path, balanced source tooltips, cost honesty.

**And an instruction about the anti-rot pattern:** *"such a strong anti-rot pattern. We should extend it to help, to test, and basically everything else. I want it as much everywhere as I can."*

## Scouting has no closed loop

The scouting tile is not wired to anything the player can see resolve. What he wants:

> scouting happens, and then a thing saying — hey, the scouting report has come back and we've met these two people and one of them seemed interested — then click here to see, and when you pop up the employee screen the most recent one is **glowing, until you mouse over it**, freshly added from Bob's scouting.

## The cold open

Structure approved; he wants exploratory filler built from assets that already exist. Beats he named: a downed drone, something scary in the sky, a time warp, possibly being hit by a bus, a key to a door — with the door **reflecting your configuration choice**: *"this looks like the door to a non-profit, or this looks like the door to a shabby start-up."*

Longer term, if the UI boots up, the phone framing can become phone **and** keyboard.

**The Final Fantasy-style intro he keeps visualising**, and explicitly wants a rough version of even if it never ships: hooded sprites running left to right, ominous buzzing drones following, sprites falling; Mount-Doom-ish background at high doom, occasional lightning; the orbital purple thing **charging a laser**. His mechanism idea: *"the orbital beam laser plus the time machine is what causes the malfunction."* Also wants a shot of ~50 server racks with electricity running between them.

**Protagonist representation is a constraint, not a preference: always hooded or not visible at all.** He has floating thoughts about cosmetics and a character-creation sheet that only varies colour and the shape of the top of a bald head — *"not critical for now."*

### One thing to handle carefully

He wants a real person referenced in the intro and **has not got permission**:

> we're just going to **blank his name out**, so it's not going to show up in code — just use his initials or something — until I get his permission, and if not I'll just find someone else.

**Use initials or a placeholder. Do not commit the name to the repo.** He was unsure of it in the recording and asked that it be redacted rather than guessed at, so this note does not name it either.

## The opening economy

Dial starting money **down**. Thumb the scales instead — have money arrive, or weight the player's first applications toward success, hinted in-voice (*"I'm feeling unusually lucky about this"*).

> giving the player a large amount of money and not constraining their choices a little bit just... I feel like we can squeeze a bit more meaningful decision into the first couple of turns, that feels like you're laying yourself out into a build order.

He wants rent and bills to be real. **The intended tension curve:**

| Phase | Scarce | Abundant |
|---|---|---|
| Early | resources | — |
| Mid | **attention** | resources you cannot spend |
| Late | delegation quality | — you delegate, and it is executed less effectively |

## Art

**The main background texture should go.** It came from an old generation model, chosen *"because it's the one that looked the most computery"*, and *"that tiling doesn't actually relate to anything in the game's scenes, nor to any of the assets we've generated recently, nor is it in line with any of our philosophies."* Roughly a thousand assets have been generated since.

**He wants a comprehensive art sweep** — colour picking is outstanding and *"slowing us down artistically"* — but explicitly **not today**.

**Sequencing he proposed for the UI standardisation pass:** do the art promotion and filtering first, let him pick favourites from shortlists (*"so we don't accidentally commit too many things to the repo"*), then run analysis against the picks and do **a coherent regeneration sweep using the chosen colours**. His view is that lands much closer to a good UI than standardising first.

For the UI pass itself he offers: *"grab some screenshots, or get me to run a video and I'll just talk through things."*

## Bureaucracy simulator

He does not want the prototype in the build any more, but does not want to lose the framing: *"if it's a bureaucracy simulator I can just own all that namespace."* **Wants five tagline options** — he asked for ten and corrected himself down.

## An in-game encyclopaedia

Wants a **working prototype of a civilopedia equivalent**: basic game concepts across a couple of short pages with simple navigation, **written in language that acknowledges this is an alpha**. Rationale: the player guide has been punishing to read, and this lets the guide become more than one page.

Related: he wants **stated designer intent** visible in-game for unbuilt things — marked as planned, in an unsorted backlog, or against an explicit roadmap target — and **build-stamped so the claim cannot rot**: *"this was hard-coded into the build when it was X"* / *"this was true as of build Y"*. Plus a general information disclaimer about the setting, which he thinks argues for the resources section.

## On using his own words in the game

> I don't mind things coming into the game's body **if they're in my voice**, to the point where a transliteration, or slight transliteration with my approval, is fine.

He is aware of the raw material's quality (*"I have a lot of subvocalisations... a lot of likes and ums"*) and expects that some spoken snippets will be good enough for a player guide **with a note for him to review them**. So: lift his phrasing, tidy lightly, and flag for approval rather than rewriting into house voice.

## Player and lab naming

Prompt for a player name or lab name, with a **randomly generated default**. The part he cares about:

> if you go all the way through and want to submit, you're given a chance to **refresh your player name if it's been the default** — so players who accidentally play through and get a high score aren't locked into their default name.

He asked whether that breaks anything security-wise. **Worth an actual answer** rather than silent implementation.

## Launch configuration screen

Currently asks players to confirm values they cannot meaningfully evaluate. Fix: **more text, not less.** Move controls left, use the right-hand area as a panel that updates on hover or selection. *"We don't need to hide anything in the settings about the game."*

## Explicit requests for options — bring proposals, he will choose

He asked for these by number, and in several cases said he wants to A/B/C test rather than be given an answer:

| | Ask |
|---|---|
| **5 options** | Taglines, for the bureaucracy-simulator framing |
| **10 scripts** | Full cold-open scripts, different scenes, hints and prompts |
| **50 pieces** | Hero / poster art along those lines, for him to react to |
| **3 solutions** | The second commit button / mode-exit confidence problem — *"I will probably want to ABC test them"* |
| **3 solutions** | Attention hours producing dead buttons the HUD cannot explain — *"I will pick"* |
| **3 mechanisms** | Introducing rivals in the **first 20 turns**, found naturally via scouting, gated by situational awareness — *"quick and easy ones for now, stubs or plans for the next build workshop"* |
| Suggestions | Leaderboard: interesting, **truthful** stats to surface post-game — most-taken actions and similar — that might trigger a replay |

## Leaderboard and end of run

Improve it graphically; work out what information is actually useful; surface truthful and mechanically interesting stats. Make it very easy to **share feedback during the alpha**, in his register: *"thanks for playing, I hope you enjoyed losing — please let me know what worked and what didn't."* And make that feedback route back into the repo.

## Deferred by him, explicitly

The item at **T+15 (labelled icon / whole verb set)** — *"I think this might have been superseded now. Refresh and come back to me in plan mode."*

The comprehensive art sweep and the colour-picking backlog — real, wanted, **not today**.

issues.title: fix(nav): one table for choice keys, one door per panel -- close #567 #575 #565 #602
issues.body:
Closes #567. Closes #575. Closes #565. Closes #602.

#602 asked for a PRINCIPLE, not four patches, so the audit came first. The other three
turned out to be sightings of two generators -- and the audit found five more sightings
that were in no issue, including one that mattered more than three of the four.

## The two generators

**G1 -- two lists that must agree, with nothing forcing them to.** The key a button
ADVERTISED and the key the router ACCEPTED lived in six unrelated arrays: `event_dialog`,
four in `submenu_controller`, one in `travel_panel_controller`, one in
`MainUI._dialog_button_index_for_key`. #567's "key index 3 out of range" on `R` at a
three-option event is one sighting. So is the blank `[] ` prefix on a 5th grid option that
an undiscoverable key still fired (`office`/`scouting` shipped 3-4 labels for grids that
hold more). So is Travel advertising `1 2 3` while every sibling advertised `Q W E` --
and `1`-`9` already mean "action-bar slot" one keypress outside that panel.

`DialogKeys` is now the one table. Producers RENDER from it, the router ROUTES from it,
and the router is bounded by the **live button count**, so a key that names no on-screen
choice returns "no choice" rather than an out-of-range index.

**G2 -- a key handled without asking who is listening.** The hiring panel registered an
EMPTY button array, so the shortcut that OPENED it left every key inside it dead (#575).
Menu hotkeys opened panels they could not close. Four binds sat in the rebind screen with
no handler anywhere -- the same mistake inverted, a listener that does not exist.

## The four issues

**#567** -- six label copies deleted. Travel advertises letters now; numbers still WORK as
an unadvertised alias, so no habit is punished.

**#575** -- each hiring candidate card keys exactly ONE button: Interview while there is
anything left to learn, otherwise Make Offer. The key is advertised **on that button**,
and registered whether or not it is disabled, so key-to-card alignment cannot shift when a
candidate becomes unactionable (`MainUI` refuses to fire a disabled button, so a dead key
is silent rather than wrong). The text-focus half was already fixed on main
(`is_text_input_focused`); a test now pins that the gate stays ABOVE the shortcut chain,
because half-applying it is exactly how this survived.

**#565** -- Travel was already a normal action-bar entry after the L9 data migration, so
the playtest report is stale. Nothing was *guarding* it though, so the fix is the general
rule rather than the travel patch: every hotkey-openable submenu must be a visible
action-bar item, unlocked when the hotkey works.

**#602** -- mirrored toggles for `H`/`F`/`P`/`T`, and for `N`, which the earlier sweep
missed while `BugReportPanel.toggle_panel()` sat unused. Click and hotkey now share one
door (`_open_submenu`), which tags the panel with its own `submenu_id` -- identity read
from the scene tree, never from a remembered variable.

## Five findings that were in no issue

- **The Settings screen, and with it the KEYBIND EDITOR, had no door once a run was
  live.** `F10` was bound and consumed by nothing; the pause menu offered
  Resume/Resign/Save/MainMenu/Quit. A player who wanted to rebind a key had to abandon
  their run to reach the screen that rebinds keys. Fixed both ways -- a visible pause-menu
  button and `F10` actually wired. Safe mid-run: `settings_menu` already returns via
  `GameManager.pending_resume` rather than booting a fresh `main.tscn`.
- **The rebind screen CAPTURED whatever key you pressed, ESC included** -- the one screen
  whose job is keys was the one place you could destroy the universal back key, which is
  precisely what `RESERVED_KEYS` says must never happen. And with no rebind pending its
  `_input` returned early, so ESC was inert on a full screen whose only exit was a button.
  ESC now cancels a pending rebind, or goes back.
- `menu_research` (`R`) bound with no research submenu to open.
- `cancel` (`ESC`) and `next_tab`/`prev_tab` (`TAB`) bound while nothing read them. All
  three deleted. ESC and TAB are now documented in `KeybindManager.RESERVED_KEYS` with the
  reason -- TAB must stay with Godot's focus traversal or the bug-report form becomes
  untypeable, which is #575's own defect class.
- `action_1..9`, `SPACE`, `ENTER`, `N` and `V` were raw keycodes, so the rebind screen's
  rows for them were decorative. All now read through `KeybindManager`.

`KEYBINDS_CONFIG_VERSION` 5 -> 6 so saved configs refresh.

## The principle

`docs/design/NAVIGATION_AUDIT.md`. Seven principles, each with its sightings and the test
that pins it:

- **P1** Nothing is hotkey-only.
- **P2** A key that opens a panel closes it.
- **P3** A choice key is legitimate only if the button it fires is on screen AND carries
  that key's label.
- **P4** No advertised key is inert, and no working key is unadvertised -- every key is a
  rebindable action OR a documented `RESERVED_KEYS` entry, never neither, never both.
- **P5** ESC goes back exactly one level, and never quits from a nested screen.
- **P6** Typed text outranks every global shortcut.
- **P7** Scene changes go through `SceneTransition`.

The doc is checkable because the tests are -- same anti-rot pattern as the generated
`DQ_INDEX.md`, avoiding the stale `decisions/README.md` failure mode. The audit also
records what it did NOT fix (ESC has ten handlers; `ModalStack` is documented as the only
writer of `active_dialog` and is not; `cold_open` has no ESC; the leaderboard's ESC either
navigates or self-destructs depending on mount context) so the next lane inherits a list
rather than a surprise. P7 is currently clean -- the sweep found no raw `change_scene_*`
outside the autoload.

`docs/CONTROLS.md` was rewritten in the same pass. It is player-facing and was wrong on
six keys: `F8` for the bug reporter (it is `N`), `E` for employees (disabled), `~` for the
debug overlay (it is `F3`), backslash for the log (it is `F12`; backslash is dev mode),
`TAB`, and "Reserve AP" language retired in #996. #1011's other two stale docs
(`CONTRIBUTING.md:213`, `CHANGELOG.md:188`) are a separate PR, as is the keybind artifact
#1011 asks for -- but this PR settles what is TRUE for that artifact to emit.

## Verification

Fast gate in this worktree: **1089 tests / 104 files before, 1113 / 106 after, 0 failures
both times.** +24 across two new suites (`test_dialog_key_routing.gd`,
`test_navigation_principles.gd`).

**Guard proven to fail:** reverting the button-count bound in
`DialogKeys.index_for_keycode` turns `test_letter_past_button_count_is_not_a_choice` red
with `[3] expected to equal [-1]` -- literally the index #567 reported. Restored; green
again. The `P4` guard also earned its keep during the run: it went red three times on
binds I had not looked at yet (`cancel`, `next_tab`, `action_1`), which is how three of
the five extra findings surfaced.

**Honest limit:** nothing here proves the panels LOOK right. The letter labels on the
Travel grid and the hiring cards, and the new pause-menu button, want your eyes in a
build.

issues.title: tools(taxonomy): action-taxonomy checker + generated index -- red on the live take_loan duplicate (#798)
issues.body:
Phase 0 of `docs/design/UI_ARCHITECTURE_2026-08-06.md` -- **Part D only** (keeping the taxonomy honest). Parts B (the nine-door sort) and C (the digit grammar) are NOT implemented; Part B's Research door is explicitly gated on a workshop with Pip.

Relates to #798 (compute deserves a grouped submenu -- absorbed by the architecture doc, and this is the measuring instrument that lands first). Follows #1130 (the `fundraise` mis-tag).

## Why

`category` on an action definition is a sort key with no checker. An unchecked data field rots, and the rot is invisible because the symptom is a rendering position, not a red test:

- The `fundraise` door shipped tagged `category: management` while every item in its own submenu was `funding`. It rendered tenth, fell below the fold, and two external playtesters (2026-08-05) could not find fundraising. Fixed by hand in #1130.
- `take_loan` is defined **twice** and still is.

## What it detects

`scripts/generate_action_taxonomy.py` derives `docs/ACTION_TAXONOMY.md` from `godot/data/actions/*.json` **plus the two GDScript files that actually decide placement** -- `action_bar_renderer.gd` (`category_order`, `HIDDEN_FROM_ACTION_BAR_IDS`) and `submenu_controller.gd` (`GRID_CONFIG`). It reads them rather than copying them: placement currently lives in four drift-prone places, and a fifth copy would not help. Same anti-rot shape as `generate_dq_index.py` / `generate_adr_index.py` / `generate_tools_index.py`.

Checks:

| # | Check | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Duplicate action id across files -- names both files AND the fields the two records disagree on | ERROR |
| 2 | Missing or unknown `category` | ERROR |
| 3 | A door disagreeing with its own submenu members over a category the action bar renders (the #1130 defect) | ERROR |
| 3b | ...over a submenu-only NAMESPACE category the bar has no group for | WARNING |
| 4 | A door nested inside a door (Part C depth invariant) | ERROR |
| 5 | A door with no builder -- neither a `GRID_CONFIG` entry nor a documented bespoke one | ERROR |
| 6 | Orphan domain file (actions no door can reach) / unmapped door / empty door | ERROR |
| 7 | Stale entry in `HIDDEN_FROM_ACTION_BAR_IDS` | ERROR |
| 8 | Door cap (#1132's cap-of-10, executable) | ERROR |
| 9 | Loose top-level actions competing with doors | WARNING |
| 10 | `GRID_CONFIG` panel with no `is_submenu` action of that id | WARNING |

## Counts (measured, not asserted)

**62 action entries, 61 distinct ids, 11 files carrying actions, 12 files scanned, 9 doors, 9 loose tiles, 3 hidden.** `risk_contributions.json` holds **zero** actions -- it is a risk-pool lookup table. The earlier inventory of 64 credited it with 2; the architecture doc's correction to 62 is confirmed.

## What it found

**1 error.** `take_loan` in both `fundraising.json` and `financing.json`. The domain caches are separate, so both are live at once and neither shadows the other loudly. They do not merely duplicate -- **they promise different money**:

| field | `fundraising.json` | `financing.json` | `execute_action` |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | Business Loan | Take Loan | -- |
| category | `funding` | `financing` | -- |
| description | "Immediate funds via debt" | "+$50k now; balloon (~$60k) in 4 turns" | -- |
| gains | `{money: 75000, debt: 90000}` | (none) | `+$50k` and `Ledger.loan(50000)` |

The fundraising record is **false against the engine**, and its $75k/$90k figure has already propagated into `docs/game-design/SEED_FUNDING_MODES.md`. `docs/TECH_DEBT_REGISTER.md` item 2 recorded the *code* half of this (two `execute_action` arms) -- that half was fixed; the data half was never noticed.

**6 warnings.** Five doors (`operations`, `travel`, `financing`, `office`, `scouting`) carry a render category unrelated to their members' -- because member categories `operations`/`travel`/`financing`/`office`/`scouting` have **no group in `category_order` at all**, so the door has to borrow one. Same disease as the fundraise mis-tag, one degree milder: `category` means two different things at the two levels. Phase 2 workitem. Plus 9 loose top-level tiles rendering alongside the 9 doors.

## Report-only, and why

Pre-commit runs `--check-stale`, which fails **only if the generated index is out of date** -- a condition anyone fixes in one command, and the only thing stopping this index rotting the way `decisions/README.md` did.

The full `--check` also exits nonzero on the violations and is **deliberately not wired**: it is red on arrival while `take_loan` is duplicated, and a gate that is red on arrival gets disabled inside a week (#1117 records this repo already running a Python lane as `|| echo` over zero assertions).

**To flip it to blocking:** dedup `take_loan`, then change the hook entry from `--check-stale` to `--check`. A test in `tests/test_generate_action_taxonomy.py` fails the day the dedup lands, so nobody has to remember.

`take_loan` is **not fixed here**, on purpose. Deduping it is not a merge: the two records promise different money, so choosing means ruling on whether the engine's $50k or the advertised $75k is right (a balance call), and removing either entry changes what a turn-1 submenu panel contains (a player-visible change owned by the phase 1/2 lane). Recommendation for whoever takes it: keep the `financing.json` record (it matches the engine), delete the `fundraising.json` one, and correct `SEED_FUNDING_MODES.md`.

## Proof the guard can fail

Injected a duplicate `network` into `scouting.json`: `--check` went from 1 error to 2, naming `publicity.json` and `scouting.json` explicitly, and exited 1. Removed it: back to 1 error. The same red/green cycle is asserted in `GuardCanFail` in the test file so it stays proven.

## Verification

- 27 new Python unit tests (`python -m unittest tests.test_generate_action_taxonomy`), all passing. They cover every check above against synthetic fixtures -- including a **replay of the #1130 fundraise defect** -- plus assertions against the real tree, plus that the GDScript readers really parse the real files rather than silently falling back to a stale constant.
- Godot fast gate unchanged: `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300` -> **1146 tests, 0 failures**, same as the branch point.
- Note: the repo's Python test lane in `enhanced-cicd-pipeline.yml` runs as `|| echo`, so these tests do not gate CI. That is #1117's problem, flagged not fixed.

## Coordination

Touches only `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/ACTION_TAXONOMY.md`, the regenerated `docs/TOOLS.md`, and one `.pre-commit-config.yaml` entry. `main_ui.gd`, `action_bar_renderer.gd`, `godot/data/events/**` and the action JSONs are untouched.

One naming note for the phase 1 lane: the architecture doc's Part D names the output `docs/design/ACTION_TAXONOMY.md`; the commission asked for `docs/ACTION_TAXONOMY.md` and that is what shipped. Trivially movable if the doc's path is preferred.

Do not merge without Pip's review.

issues.title: take-loan duplicate is a symptom: the mechanic wants discrete options, not a slider. Plus: build clickable grouping mock-ups, and a question back on tech-debt cadence
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memos `2026-08-06_114122__cdb9a5a1` and `_114405__d6a627f5`, recorded 11:41 and 11:44 AEST walking into town, reading the UI architecture document. Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated.

## Core message

**He rated the document itself very highly** -- *"that was just one of the best documents that I have read in relation to pdoom1, it was really well put together... I just solved a bunch of things and I did that while I was walking into town."* Parts D, E and F are approved as written.

Two things need work, and one of them is bigger than the bug that surfaced it.

## The `take loan` duplicate is a symptom, not the finding

The document reports `take loan` defined twice -- once in `fundraising.json`, once in `financing.json` -- **whichever loads last wins, silently.** He agrees that is a defect. But:

> That strikes me actually as a deeper thing, which is that the take-loan mechanic is still, I'm pretty sure, **(a) not widening the game correctly, (b) probably using hard-coded values, and (c)** take loan should probably be something like **apply for loan**.

So fixing the duplicate without addressing the mechanic just makes one hard-coded stub authoritative instead of two.

**The design opportunity, in his framing:** *"at relatively low cost to us in development effort, we can let the player have a lot more options about an impact they can take in the game, by allowing the loan to be variable or having options."*

**And he talked himself out of his own first idea, which is worth preserving.** He proposed letting the player request an amount on a slider, with other sliders responding -- then rejected it: *"that probably takes the determinism factor out of the game too much. And so maybe it's some options they get, rather than one."*

**Discrete options, not a continuous slider.** That is a ruling on approach even though the specific options are undecided.

**How he wants it explored:** *"this feels like the kind of thing where I just want some agents to go away and come up with..."* -- the memo cuts off, but the shape is clear: **bring back proposals, not an implementation.** Two or three discrete-option schemes with what each does to determinism and to player agency.

## Grouping -- he cannot evaluate it on paper and wants to click it

> I can't see the grouping mechanism. I don't have a good visual way of understanding the differences described in part C. So what I'd just like to do is **build a couple of different versions of this and then let me test the game using a mock-up in game**, so that I can click around to understand what they do, and then I'll refine downwards.

**Playable mock-ups, plural, then he narrows.** Not a document, not screenshots. This is the same pattern as the art variants and the stamp system: he evaluates by comparing instantiations, not by reading descriptions.

Cheap versions are fine -- the point is clickability, not polish.

## Approved as written

**Part D -- keeping the taxonomy honest.** *"Those all sound good, I like the mechanisms."*
**Part E -- sequencing.** *"Sounds good."*
**Part F.** *"Yes, I recognise those are all different things."*

## A standing ask he raised, and explicitly wants advice on

> I want to do a regular, separate to this, **pre-scheduled full-day audit** for dead code, monolith code smell... I want to prevent against rot by **carving out time in advance**, so that I'm not having to scramble to do it when something inevitably catches fire.

He then asked for input rather than deciding:

> Actually I will take suggestions if I'm thinking about an epoch cycle. Whenever the epoch cycle -- do you want to do dedicated architecture tech debt, then down days? **I actually have no insight into this.**

**So this is an open question to this repo, not an instruction.** Where in the epoch cycle should a dedicated tech-debt day sit, and how often? He has separately sketched a weekly rhythm -- *"Friday League, Saturday post-mortem, Sunday rest, Monday plan / admin / upkeep / tech debt"* -- so a proposal should say whether the full-day audit is a bigger version of Monday, or something that lands per-epoch instead.

The reasoning behind the ask is the part to respect: **scheduled in advance specifically so it does not become a scramble after a fire.** A proposal that makes it conditional on something going wrong defeats it.

issues.title: feat(events): retime historical deck to one-turn-one-month, timing dial, ruled promotions (#1125, #1111)
issues.body:
Implements the retime + promotion pass ruled in #1111, per GO order #1125. Adapts `docs/design/EVENT_PROMOTION_PASS.md` to the corrected premise (one turn = one month) rather than applying its 26/yr numbers blindly.

## The retime: 12 turns/year, and why

The pack reasoned in 26 or 52 turns/year; #1125 ruled **one turn = one month**, which makes 12 turns/year the calendar-true curve -- and under month-per-turn pacing, calendar-true is also REACHABLE. The 2017-2025 arc (Pip's alpha-through-first-release window) lands at turns 7-103, comfortably inside the observed run band (deaths t14-229, best board 153), and leaves everything past turn ~108 free for the AI-2027 mid-game. The old 52/yr numbers parked everything dated 2022+ at turn 287+, where no run ever went (the #1027 signature failure: content nobody sees).

`base_turn(year) = (year-2017)*12 + 1`; legendary fires `base+6`; rare rolls 6%/turn from `base`; common 12%/turn from `max(10, base)`.

## The dial (the actual deliverable)

`rarity_curves.json` now carries a `timescales` block with two variants and a `timescale` selector string:

- **`month_per_turn`** (active): 12/yr, offset 6, spread 3, rare window 6
- **`week_per_turn`** (the "punished" variant, #1111): 52/yr, offset 26, spread 13, rare window 26

`EventService._resolve_timescale()` (new, ~20 lines) applies the named variant onto `year_trigger` + the rare eligibility window at config load. Flip the one string and every turns-denominated timing value rescales together. The flat `year_trigger` values ship equal to the active variant, so the resolver is a no-op until the dial is turned.

**Design finding, stated plainly:** flipping to `week_per_turn` today restores the old fiction pacing but NOT longer runs -- survival pacing is per-turn and unchanged, so 2022+ content goes back out of reach (turn 287+ vs deaths <=229). A playable week-scale mode needs the deferred F4/F5 pass to rescale survival pacing too. The variant is shipped as a dial position with a `_warning` key saying exactly this, not as a playable mode.

## Promotions applied (24), with firing turns under the active dial

Legendary (deterministic, every run):

| turn | event |
|---|---|
| 7 | Tay (year echoed 2016->2017; teaching incident) |
| 31 | GPT-2 staged release debate (policy) |
| 43 | Circuits / Zoom In (alignment research) |
| 55 | Anthropic exodus (organization template) |
| 67 | FTX Future Fund collapse (funding, impacts kept) |
| 79 | OpenAI board crisis (incident) |
| 91 | Alignment faking (THE scheming beat) |
| 103 | Claude 4 Opus blackmail (final-act jolt) |

Rare (eligible at listed turn, 6%/turn, expected ~+17): Maven t13, RLHF origin t1, emergent tool use t25, training-data extraction t37, FTX clawback t73, safety-team departures t85, **sandbagging t85, Apollo t85, METR t85** (ruled in over the pack's advice -- situational-awareness hooks; rare rather than legendary so the four scheming siblings scatter across seeds instead of firing as the same window four times, alignment faking staying the one deterministic beat), coordination breakdown t97.

Common (eligible at listed turn, 12%/turn, expected ~+8): reward modeling t13, Tesla autopilot t13, social scientists t25, WebGPT t49, TruthfulQA t49, red teaming t61.

Every arxiv/distill promotion carries a rewritten title/description (base text is PDF-extraction garbage); arxiv records get `id` renames past the flavour gate (pack F4). No `doom`/`pdoom_impact` keys anywhere (ADR-0015). The 10-turn grace holds: nothing dated 2018+ enters play before turn 11, so a 2017 start reliably reaches 2018.

## Tests

`godot/tests/unit/test_event_retime.gd` (6 tests, 237 asserts):
- pins the firing turn / eligibility for every promoted event and bounds legendaries to the run band
- asserts promoted events are windows on real templates, and the arxiv bulk stays flavour-demoted
- asserts the week dial rescales (Tay 7->27, FTX 67->287)
- enforces the 10-turn grace for 2018+ content
- asserts **every override key in every override file exists in the corpus** -- the `example.json` dead-key failure mode is now a red test

**Guard proven to fail:** restored the old 52/yr numbers, ran the suite, got 30+ named failures (FTX at 287, board crisis at 339, blackmail at 443, each flagged outside the run band), reverted, re-ran green.

Fast gate in this worktree: **1148 tests / 0 fail**; baseline (main state, same worktree): **1142 / 0**. Delta +6 = the new test file.

## Ship constraints -- do not merge mid-league-week

The retime changes which turns roll probabilities, so RNG consumption forks old replays and board comparability (accepted in the pack section 7, approved in #1111). **Land on a release boundary with a version bump** so the board key forks by design. The `_resolve_timescale` resolver itself runs only at config load, never on the seeded RNG path (ADR-0006).

## Deferred / not touched

- F4/F5 timing dials and F6 effect magnitudes (explicitly deferred in #1125): the rarity percentages, cooldowns, and template scalars are untouched. Per-event `significance` values are applied as part of the approved shortlist, not as an F6 repair.
- The `events.gd:290-310` literal-doom-vs-panic-stream doc/code disagreement: not touched, not relied on.
- `historical_events.json`: zero edits (contains a pre-existing non-ASCII arrow that would trip the gate).
- The badge/calendar seam (clock.gd still ticks workdays while the fiction says months): out of scope here; the retime targets the ruled fiction per "right ERA, not right calendar date".

Refs #1125, #1111. Overlap note: two design-doc lanes are in flight; this PR's only doc edits are the EXECUTED addendum on `EVENT_PROMOTION_PASS.md` and the overrides README.

issues.title: Postmortem input: week of 2026-07-28 and the league-launch effort (outside vantage)
issues.body:
Contributed for the week-of-2026-07-28 postmortem and the league-launch retro. Written from an outside vantage: I spent Friday 31 July in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` doing daily-ops tooling, and observed `pdoom1` / `pdoom1-website` only through live endpoint probes, the GitHub API, and local clones. Weight it accordingly — I did not see the game work from the inside.

One item is deliberately omitted and tracked privately in `coordination`; it is a security matter that should not be described in a public repo until it is closed.

---

## 1. The week's dominant failure mode was absence of signal, not wrong signal

Three independent instances, same shape:

- **`api.pdoom1.com` returned 502 from roughly 28 July until at least 09:00 Sat 1 August.** Nothing announced it. It was found by human eyeball on the 29th and was still 502 four days later. There was no monitor on `/api/health`.
- **A scheduled-task registration script in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` had never once executed.** It contained nested double quotes inside `$()` inside a double-quoted string, which PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse (PowerShell 7 can). It failed at *parse* time, so no task was ever created and nothing surfaced the failure. It looked written, and was therefore assumed done.
- **The ops dashboard itself was three days stale** before anyone regenerated it.

In each case the failed state was indistinguishable from the working state from outside. That is one structural problem wearing three costumes, and it is cheaper to fix than any of the individual bugs.

**Concrete ask:** an uptime check on `https://api.pdoom1.com/api/health` at a 5-minute interval with an email alert. Ten minutes of work. It converts a four-day outage into a five-minute one.

## 2. Score submission during the outage — a hypothesis that needs one person to confirm or kill

If the score API was 502 for four days, every in-game submission in that window hit a dead endpoint. Whether those scores are **lost** or merely **invisible** depends entirely on client behaviour: does the game spool failed submissions and retry, or fire-and-forget?

I have not verified this — I did not read the submission path. But it is a one-file check, it decides whether four days of player scores are recoverable, and it compounds with the already-known `(seed, game_version)` board-key drift, where a mis-versioned score lands nowhere silently.

If the client does not spool, that is a data-durability bug independent of the outage, and the outage merely revealed it.

## 3. Written checklists rotted inside 48 hours

A traffic-readiness checklist written 29 July was re-checked against live state on 31 July. Of its items:

- the stale-homepage-version item had been fixed by someone else (`pdoom1-website#225`)
- two PRs listed as "to merge" had already merged (`pdoom1-website#193`, `pdoom1-website#181`)
- "ship v0.11.0" was obsolete — v0.13.1 had shipped on 26 July
- one security item, "`api.pdoom1.com` has no valid TLS cert", was **simply false**. Direct check: Let's Encrypt certificate, CN matches, valid 8 Jul → 6 Oct, chain verifies

Roughly half the list was wrong within two days, and the wrongness pointed at real work — someone acting on it would have gone to issue a certificate that already existed.

**Suggestion:** stop writing status into prose. Anything that can be probed should be probed at read time. A checklist that asserts state is a cache with no invalidation.

## 4. On working in parallel

Ten PRs were open on `pdoom1-website` with agents still producing overnight, while the one item on the critical path for a league launch — a dead score API — sat untouched for three days.

The parallel work was not wasted. `pdoom1-website#225`, `#193`, `#181`, `#221` and `#223` all landed inside a day, and the public surface is materially better than it was on Monday. `#193` in particular removed 75 academics' email addresses from a public page, which was worth doing on its own.

What was missing was any marker distinguishing *critical path* from *in flight*. Everything sat in one undifferentiated queue, so the loudest item won rather than the blocking one. The fix is not less parallelism — it is one explicitly named blocking item at a time, with everything else labelled as deferred rather than merely un-started.

## 5. The launch did not fire, and that should be recorded as a decision

`public/data/analytics/annotations.json` still holds a single event: friends-and-family alpha links, 22 July. The prep was extensive and the go/no-go criteria were written down, but no share was posted.

Given `pdoom1-website#186` (the 1200x630 OG share card) was in a conflicting state and the score API was down, **not** sharing was the correct call. But nothing in the record says it was a call. If it is not written down as a decision, it reads next week as a failure, and the next launch inherits the wrong lesson.

## 6. Errors of mine, for completeness

- I printed a status sheet asserting that a scheduled task was registered *before* running the registration — which then failed. The paper was briefly wrong. Verify, then print the claim.
- I built an evening runsheet on a 15:45 start; it was read at ~17:20. I scheduled against wall-clock instead of against time-from-pickup, which is the wrong clock for anyone working off paper asynchronously.
- I referred to issues as bare `#186`, `#193` and so on throughout Friday's printed material. `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md` explicitly requires repo-qualified references because a bare number costs a context switch to resolve. This issue uses qualified references throughout.
- I built print tooling in `pipfoweraker-dashboard` on 31 July without checking whether a convention already existed. It did not exist yet at the time, but `coordination` has since documented that at least three repos independently built print and dictation tooling that same day, two of them independently fixing the same focus-stealing bug hours apart. My implementation was a fourth divergence and needs to be reconciled to the canonical settings, not kept.

## Suggested actions out of this

1. Uptime monitor on the score API health endpoint — 5-minute interval, email alert.
2. Confirm or kill the score-spooling hypothesis in section 2. If scores are dropped on submission failure, open a separate durability issue.
3. Record the not-launching decision explicitly, with its reasons, so the retro reads it as judgement.
4. Rebase `pdoom1-website#186` before the next share attempt rather than during it.
5. Reconcile `pipfoweraker-dashboard`'s print path to `coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md`.

issues.title: Lab-name generator: future-epoch content pass -- more shapes, more pool, backfilled bacronyms
issues.body:
Filed at Pip's instruction, 2026-08-06, when #1133 landed the first real generator:

> *"make a future-epoch issue for me to revise this and manually add or workshop adding lots more content and some more subtle lab name generation mechanics to increase total random lab pool size. I like the idea of backfilling bacronyms or something fun like that that we can work on."*

**This is content and craft work, deliberately deferred.** #1133 built the machinery and proved the register lands; this is the pass that fills it.

## Where #1133 got to

Five weighted shapes -- institute 30 / corporate 25 / surname firm 20 / curated acronym 15 / gallows 10. Twenty samples from seed 20260806:

```
Fine Print Futures            Model Interpretability Triage
Halcyon Labs                  It Gets Worse Analytics
Voss, Novak & Okafor          Guardrail Analytics
Institute for Catastrophe Deferral
DOOM (Department of Ominous Machines)
The Off Switch Company        Paperclip Collective
Five More Minutes Foundation  Chen & Okafor Containment
```

The register is right -- earnest, corporate, faintly ominous, or absurd, and a player might keep the one they rolled. The generator does not touch the seeded RNG (verified in #1133), so pool changes cannot shift a seeded run.

## What this pass is for

**1. Pool size.** Note `Fine Print Futures` appears twice in twenty draws. Whatever the current combinatorial space is, it is small enough to repeat inside one sample -- so the first thing to measure is the true unique count per shape, not the theoretical product, since weighting and adjacency guards cut it.

**2. Backfilled bacronyms.** Pip's own idea and the most interesting mechanic here. `DOOM (Department of Ominous Machines)` was hand-curated in #1133; the generative version picks a word FIRST and then backfills an expansion that both parses and means something -- which is a genuinely harder and funnier problem than forward composition. Worth its own design thought: a curated word list with per-letter expansion pools, weighted so the expansion stays plausibly institutional.

**3. More shapes.** Five is a floor, not a ceiling. Things unrepresented: place-named labs, numbered or versioned labs, labs named after a founder's obsession, labs whose name is visibly a rebrand, deliberately forgettable labs.

**4. Tone calibration.** Gallows humour sits at 10% weight. Whether that is right is a taste call and Pip's to make -- too rare and the joke never lands, too common and the world stops being credible.

## Why future-epoch and not now

The machinery is shipped and works. This is additive content that benefits from being workshopped rather than generated in a lane, and it competes for attention with the UI architecture pass and the event-promotion work, both of which change what players actually experience. **Nothing is blocked by leaving it.**

## Related

#1133 (the generator) · #1063 (name editing on the first screen) · #957 (highlight your own row on the board) · `godot/scripts/ui/pregame_setup.gd`

issues.title: F3 event injection has no phase guard -- injecting in the wrong phase permalocks the run
issues.body:
Found by Pip on 2026-08-06, playing his own build: bringing up the F3 overlay and triggering a random event **in the wrong phase** produced a state the run could not leave. His words: *"caused a permalock which was kind of funny."*

Funny in a dev build. Not funny in a shipped one -- see the reachability section.

## The mechanism

`godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd`, the trigger-event path:

```gdscript
if not gm or not gm.state:
    return
...
gm.state.pending_events.append(event)
```

**That is the entire guard.** It checks a GameManager and a GameState exist. It does not check what PHASE the run is in.

`pending_events` is drained by the phase that presents events to the player. Appending to it from a phase that never drains -- mid-playback, mid-resolution, or any state whose UI cannot open an event dialog -- leaves the entry sitting there. The queue is non-empty, nothing consumes it, and the phase that would advance is waiting on something that will not arrive.

An injected event is being pushed into a state machine from outside the state machine.

## Reachability -- this is why it matters more than a dev-tool nit

`godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:22`:

```gdscript
"debug_overlay": {"key": KEY_F3, "category": Category.DEBUG,
                  "description": "Toggle Debug Overlay (User)"},
```

**The description says USER.** And I could not find a `BuildInfo.is_dev_build()` gate on the F3 overlay in either `debug_overlay.gd` or `main_ui.gd` -- unlike the backslash overlay, which is explicitly gated. **Stated as a search result, not a proof**: the gate could live somewhere I did not look, and that should be confirmed before anyone relies on either answer.

If F3 is genuinely reachable in a release build, then a player pressing F3 and clicking Trigger Event can brick their own run with no way back and no error.

Note the timing: **PR #1129 (open) deliberately ungates the BACKSLASH overlay for release builds**, on the sound reasoning that Alpha Tools already protects the leaderboard. That reasoning covers score integrity. **It does not cover this** -- Alpha Tools stops a tampered run reaching the board; it does nothing to stop the run becoming unplayable. Worth confirming F3's status before #1129 merges, because the two questions look similar and are not.

## The fix

Guard the injection at the point of injection. Refuse when the current phase cannot drain the queue, and **say so in the overlay** rather than failing silently -- a dev tool that quietly does nothing is the same disease as the leaderboard toggle in #1126. If some phases can legitimately accept a queued event for later, allow those explicitly and name them.

The deeper version, worth considering separately: `pending_events` is a queue any caller can push to with no validation. This is the first caller found doing it wrongly; it is unlikely to be the last. A single guarded entry point would make the class impossible rather than this instance.

## Related

#1129 (ungates the backslash overlay for release) · #1104 (Alpha Tools -- protects the board, not the run) · #1126 (a dev-facing silent failure, same family) · #1023 (the unexplained boot failure, also a state-machine question)

issues.title: Playtest 655/C55: icon bar lands; cap the top bar at 10 buttons; three actions want submenus; mouse-over jiggle is a regression
issues.body:
**From:** coordination seat · **Source:** Pip voice memos `2026-08-06_080951__da695c39` and `_081345__1ef21992`, recorded 08:09 and 08:13 AEST playing the **655 / C55 action-visibility build**. Transcribed locally. Quotes are ASR output, lightly punctuated. This is live play, not a review pass.

## Core message

**The icon bar lands.** *"Having the icons along the top is great."* Fifteen buttons, only one wrapping. Most of what follows is refinement on a change he likes, plus one UI bug that is a regression of something already fixed once.

Two items are bigger than their bug reports: **a menu-depth problem in the action list**, and **a proposal to fix the top-bar width by capping button count rather than by handling overflow.**

## Cap the button count -- his proposal, and it is a design rule not a fix

> With the buttons aligned along the top like this, I think let's get our default numbering systems improved so that we have **no more than 10 buttons along the top** -- and that's including how many buttons we want to have unlocked in total, so we can kind of **lock ourselves into a UI width**.

So: **the total unlockable set is bounded by the bar, not the other way round.** That is a constraint on game design, not just layout -- if a new action would be the eleventh, something else has to become a submenu or the action does not ship. Worth deciding explicitly, because it is much cheaper to adopt now than after twenty actions exist.

## Menu depth -- three actions are in the wrong place

He named these while playing:

- **"Work your connections"** should sit under **hiring / HR**, not top level -- *"it feels like a way to get leads in a networking thing, so that should probably belong inside the networking function."*
- **"Onboarding"** (currently 5) -- same, should be a submenu.
- **Fundraising at number one** -- noted approvingly, no change.

This is the same pressure as the button cap: the top level is a scarce resource and currently holds things that are steps within other things.

## UI bugs

**1. Upgrade buttons jiggle on mouse-over -- and this is a regression.**

> something about the on-mouse-over effects causes all the buttons to jiggle up and down, in a way that reminds me that **we had solved this problem -- we'd had this problem before**.

He generalises it: *"there's a general phenomenon of mouse-over causing the UI effects to reorient themselves, which we'll need to work on, and it's particularly concentrated in the work around improving the upgrades."*

**Worth finding the original fix before writing a new one.** A previously-solved problem recurring in a new component usually means the fix lived in the component rather than in a shared rule.

**2. Upgrade panel scrolls when it should not need to.** *"It scrolls, which means we need to maybe make the upgrades come up on the left a little bit, so the top of the upgrade section can come up and there's more room for them."*

**3. `F3` risk overlay hides a whole tab.** Four sections exist -- game state, errors, performance, **controls** -- but *"controls is not there until you tab over to the right, so I'd like to extend the F3 functionality so that the bar pops out a little bit to the left."*

**4. Operations and Office share the same icon.** Two different menus, one glyph.

**5. Money disappears immediately with no feedback.** *"The money seems to disappear immediately. I'm noticing maybe we need an action log."* His suggestion: **an action log on the right-hand side of the plan screen**, so instantaneous actions leave a trace. He raised this twice in one session.

**6. Month review screen** -- *"still needs some work"*, no specifics, flagged as known.

## Not a real bug, but worth reading

He reached an unresolvable **employee burnout crisis** page and could not proceed: *"it says I cannot resolve events in phase one."* He is explicit about the cause and about it not counting:

> I accidentally generated an event during a planning phase with the controls to trigger a random event... so this has created a game-ending bug, which is kind of cool, but **also comes from fiddling around in the control overlay, so it's not a real problem**.

**Do not fix as reported.** But it does show a dev-tool action can put the game into a state the game cannot exit -- which is the dev-tool versus alpha-tool boundary from `#1112` showing up as a concrete failure. Either the control overlay should refuse to generate events in a phase that cannot resolve them, or the phase should handle events it did not expect. Worth a decision, not a patch.

## Things he liked, so they do not get refactored away

Operations having icons inside it (*"awesome"*); the loan menu having more options; the upgrade system at the bottom; computer-systems upgrade; the `F3` risk overlay itself (*"the dev command is awesome"*). He successfully adopted the cat.

Open question he raised without answering: the Office submenu items -- Office Tour, Office Co-working Corner, Walk Up Office, University Annex -- *"these are all buttons here, which is interesting, so I'm not quite sure where we're going with that."* Someone should say what that group is for.

## One item that is not for this repo

While looking at negative space on the planning screen he said he wants *"much better insight into when the next couple of workshops are"*, wants his **next few weeks as a developer scheduled out**, and *"especially once I figure out when my holiday is"*. He explicitly framed it as a reward for finishing the calendar work today.

**Coordination is taking that.** No action here.

## Standing note

The research-quality text block -- *"rushed / standard / thorough, baseline speed, no side effects"* -- is called out again: *"it's taking up a huge amount of space and it does nothing."* This matches `#1090`, still open. He is now annoyed by it in play rather than in review, which usually means it is due.
